lines: Description:
Run AI-powered multi-agent security audit on a Symfony project
Usage:
audit:run [options] [--] [<project-path>]
audit
Arguments:
project-path                               Path to the Symfony project to audit. Defaults to the current working directory.
Options:
-f, --format=FORMAT                        Output format: console, executive, json, sarif, html, markdown, junit or github [default: "console"]
-o, --output=OUTPUT                        Output file path (any format)
--dry-run                              Estimate token usage and cost without invoking the LLM; emits a report with zero vulnerabilities and an estimated cost block.

--show-scanned                         List the files that would be audited (after applying included_paths and any --path filters) and exit, without invoking the LLM. Use it to confirm your scan scope. Combine with --dry-run to also print the cost estimate.

--no-cache                             Bypass the attacker and reviewer caches for this run: skip cache reads so every chunk and verdict hits the LLM, and skip cache writes so existing entries stay untouched. Useful after upgrading the auditor or when you need to force a fresh analysis.

-p, --path=PATH                            Restrict the scan to a subdirectory of the project (relative to the project root). Repeat the option to include several subdirectories. Useful for monorepos where only one app should be audited. By default the whole project is scanned. (multiple values allowed)

--since=SINCE                          Diff mode: audit only files changed against the given git ref (e.g. main, origin/main, abc1234). Honors both committed changes (ref...HEAD) and uncommitted working-tree changes. Designed for CI on pull requests; the cache stays warm for unchanged files.

--baseline=BASELINE                    Baseline file of accepted-finding fingerprints. Findings whose fingerprint is listed are suppressed from the report and excluded from the exit code. Overrides the audit.baseline config key. A missing file suppresses nothing.

--generate-baseline=GENERATE-BASELINE  Run the audit, then write every current finding fingerprint to the given file as a baseline and exit 0 without failing on findings (3 under --fail-on-incomplete when some file could not be fully analyzed; a run with no verdict writes no baseline and exits 1). Use this to accept the current findings so future runs only report new ones.

--fail-on=FAIL-ON                      Minimum aggregate risk level (safe|low|medium|high|critical) that makes the command exit 1. Overrides the audit.fail_on config key for this run. Defaults to the configured value (critical) when omitted.

--min-score=MIN-SCORE                  Minimum normalized score (0-100) below which the command exits 1. Independent of --fail-on: the audit fails when either gate trips. Omit to gate on the risk level alone.

--fail-on-incomplete                   Exit 3 when some file could not be fully analyzed (a scan or LLM call failed), so a partial report cannot pass CI. A tripped --fail-on or --min-score gate still exits 1. Without it, such a run only prints a warning.
-h, --help                                 Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command
--silent                               Do not output any message
-q, --quiet                                Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed
-V, --version                              Display this application version
--ansi|--no-ansi                       Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output
-n, --no-interaction                       Do not ask any interactive question
-v|vv|vvv, --verbose                       Increase the verbosity of messages: 1 for normal output, 2 for more verbose output and 3 for debug
Help:
The audit:run command runs a multi-agent LLM security audit against a Symfony project.
By default it audits the current working directory; pass a path to audit a different project (e.g. symfony-security-auditor audit:run /path/to/project).
Output formats (--format, -f):
console  human-readable summary (default)
executive stakeholder summary — risk level, business impact, severity/type/hotspot distributions, no per-finding detail
json     machine-readable report
sarif    SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub Code Scanning / GitLab Security Dashboard
html     self-contained HTML report for sharing or archiving
markdown Markdown report for a PR comment or GitHub step summary
junit    JUnit XML — findings as failed test cases for CI test-report panels (e.g. GitLab free-tier MR widgets)
github   GitHub Actions workflow-command annotations — inline findings on the PR's Files Changed view
Use --output (-o) to write the report to a file:
symfony-security-auditor audit:run --format=sarif --output=report.sarif
symfony-security-auditor audit:run --format=html --output=report.html
Baseline (suppress accepted findings):
symfony-security-auditor audit:run --generate-baseline=.security-baseline.json  accept current findings
symfony-security-auditor audit:run --baseline=.security-baseline.json           suppress them on later runs
Baselined findings are dropped from the report and do not affect the exit code.
Exit codes (the failure threshold is configurable via audit.fail_on / --fail-on, default critical;
--min-score adds a second, independent gate — the audit fails when either one trips):
0  audit completed; risk level is below the fail-on threshold and the score is at or above --min-score
1  audit completed with risk level at or above the fail-on threshold, or a score below --min-score, or the audit itself failed,
or the run reached no verdict (its scan found no file, or it analyzed none and found nothing)
2  audit budget could not be honored: it aborted mid-run because the configured token or cost budget was
exceeded (partial report still emitted), or it never started because an unpriced model makes the cost
budget unenforceable and the run was declined or non-interactive (no report emitted in that case)
3  --fail-on-incomplete is set and some file could not be fully analyzed (a tripped gate still exits 1);
without the option, a run that analyzed some of its files or holds a finding keeps the code its gates earn
and prints a warning
Cost & duration: a typical Symfony project (~150 files) takes minutes, not seconds,
and costs a few cents to a few dollars depending on the selected model. Configure
via config/packages/symfony_security_auditor.yaml.

Configuration : docs/configuration.md
